chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan al-Isbahani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Blessed is every obscure servant, who is not sought after by people; he knows people, but people do not know him. Allah recognizes him with pleasure. Those are the lanterns of guidance; every dark trial is lifted from them, and the door of every mercy is opened for them. They are not the boastful show-offs, nor the quarrelsome hypocrites.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Speak good, so you will be recognized by it, and do good, so you will be among its people, and do not be hasty show-offs. Indeed, the best of you are those who, when looked at, Allah is remembered; and the worst of you are the gossipers, the separators between loved ones, the seekers of faults of the righteous.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best and worst people according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 98 on Concealment (al-Khumūl), this hadith highlights the spiritual merit of obscurity, where the believer remains known to Allah while avoiding the vanity of public recognition. It contrasts the 'best' of the community, whose mere presence evokes God's remembrance, with the 'worst,' characterized by gossip (namīmah) and division, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner purity over outward status.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al Hassan Al Isbahany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Touba (a tree in Paradise) is for every obscure servant. It is irrelevant whether the people know him or they do not know him (famous or not). Allahazwj does Recognise him from them with Pleasure. They are the lanterns of guidance. Every dark strife brightens up from them, and the door of every Mercy opens up for them. They are neither with the broadcasting of the seeding (imparted knowledge), nor are they with the quarrelsome hypocrites’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Speak well, you will be recognised by it, and do good works, you would become from its rightful ones, and do not become hasty broadcasters, for the best ones of you are those who whey they are looked at, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is remembered; and the most evil ones of you are the slanderers with the gossip, the separators between the loved ones, the seekers of the faults of the righteous ones’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu al- Hassan al-Asbahani from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘Tuba’ (a tree in paradise) is for every servant (of Allah) who is unnoticed among the people but knows people and they do not know him. Allah knows him from His side with happiness. They are the torches of guidance. Through them every darkening calamity is removed aside and for them every door to blessing opens. They do not publicize undisclosed facts and they are not quarrelsome braggarts.’

He has also said, ‘Speak of the good so you become known for it. Do good and be of its people and do not be hastening announcers. The best of you are those who on looking up on them one is reminded of Allah and the wicked ones among you are those who publicize undisclosed facts, cause separation among the loved ones and search for faults in the innocent people.’”
